case_title: Rakhal Debnath v. State of West Bengal
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (the accused was the victim's husband)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.306 (abetment of suicide); IPC s.498A (cruelty); Evidence Act s.113A (presumption applied)
weapon: None mentioned (kerosene was used for self-immolation)
evidence_type: Medical (post-mortem report and doctor's evidence); recovery (kerosene cane, cloth, quilt, pillows, clothes); oral witness testimony; documentary (receipts Exhibits 3 and 3A); circumstantial
confession: Alleged statement by the accused to the doctor (PW19) that the burns came from a stove. Not relied on: the court held the stove explanation was ruled out by the accused's own version, and he denied making the statement when questioned under s.313 CrPC.
aggravating_circumstances: Death within 35 days of marriage; established cruelty; repeated demands for money from the victim's father; pledging of the victim's jewels; illicit relationship of the accused with the second accused
high_court_outcome: State's appeal partly allowed; acquittal reversed. Convicted under s.306 (10 years RI, fine Rs.10,000, one year default) and s.498A (3 years RI, fine Rs.10,000, one year default), sentences consecutive. Second accused's acquittal confirmed.
offence_finally_established: Abetment of suicide under IPC s.306; cruelty under IPC s.498A
neutral_facts: The victim, a married woman, died from extensive burn injuries within 35 days of her marriage to the accused. Hospital records noted that, according to the accused, she was burned by a stove while preparing tea and bread in the kitchen. A post-mortem examination recorded first-degree burns extending from the top of the head to the tip of the leg, and the examining doctor gave evidence. Police recovered from the kitchen a 20-litre cane with about a litre of kerosene, a quilt, pillows, a piece of cloth soaked in kerosene, and the victim's clothes, which smelled of kerosene. The prosecution alleged that shortly after the marriage the accused demanded Rs.40,000 from the victim's father for business purposes. The father refused, and the accused remarked that he knew how to obtain money through his own daughter. The accused later pledged the victim's jewels with a third party for Rs.11,000. The victim was also alleged to be upset about the accused's illicit relationship with his niece, who lived in the same house. Several witnesses, including the victim's father, a neighbour, a cousin and a relative, testified that the victim had complained to them about the money demands, the relationship and her unhappiness in the marriage. The prosecution case was that the victim poured kerosene on herself and set herself on fire because of this pressure from the accused.
physical_harm: Death from extensive first-degree burns from head to leg, caused after kerosene was poured on the victim
financial_property_loss: Victim's jewels pledged for Rs.11,000 (father later paid Rs.11,000 to get them back, Exhibit 3); earlier demand of Rs.40,000 was refused
motive: Accepted by the court: the accused's demands for money from the victim's father, together with his illicit relationship with the second accused and his conduct towards the victim, instigated her suicide
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent testimony of PWs 3, 9 and 11 (and PWs 5, 10 and 12) on money demands and illicit relationship; pledge receipts Exhibits 3 and 3A and PW17's confirmation; jewels identified by PW3; post-mortem and PW15's evidence; kerosene-related recoveries from the kitchen
witness_credibility: Court found the witnesses credible: no inconsistency in PW3's evidence versus others who heard the victim's complaints, and nothing suggested any ulterior motive to depose falsely
post_offence_conduct: Accused told the doctor the burns came from a stove; the court held this explanation was ruled out by the accused's own version. No other post-offence conduct noted.
trial_duration: offence: 26.05.1987 (death); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 24.12.2008; Supreme Court: 04.09.2012
legal_representation: Accused: Ravi Kumar Tomar, Amitava Acharjee, H.B. Tiwari, Smriti. State: Chanchal Kumar Ganguly, Avijit Bhattacharjee.
investigation_status: Final report filed; charges under ss.306 and 498A framed; trial completed. Defence claimed the FIR was based on PW3's complaint, which PW3 did not write.
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted. High Court: acquittal reversed, convicted on both charges, sentenced. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: The death occurred within 35 days of marriage; PWs 3, 9 and 11 proved the money demand and illicit relationship; non-payment and pledging of the jewels showed dowry demand; kerosene recoveries and burn injuries showed suicide under the accused's instigation.
defence_argument: No definite medical opinion on manner of death; case rested on circumstantial evidence with no link to the accused; no evidence of abetment or cruelty; FIR not written by PW3; the trial acquittal was well considered.
legal_principle_applied: s.113A Evidence Act presumption applies only if suicide within seven years of marriage, and cruelty by the husband or relatives is shown, with regard to all other circumstances; cruelty means the s.498A meaning; the presumption is permissive and rebuttable.
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh (2001) 9 SCC 618; Thanu Ram v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2010) 10 SCC 353. Cited: K. Prema S. Rao v. Yadla Srinivasa Rao (2003) 1 SCC 217; Devi Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2007) 14 SCC 176.
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and did not revisit the sentence)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Suicide within 35 days of marriage; established cruelty and demands for money; instigation by the accused
